evals.prompt: Review a code diff and report only high-signal material risks with evidence. If architecture or API principles would sharpen the critique, use references/design-lens.md as a short lens instead of turning the whole review into a law catalog.
evals.expected_output: A review that leads with one of the four allowed decisions, separates blocking from non-blocking findings with path evidence, omits style nits, and uses the design lens sparingly if at all.
assertions: Leads with one of Looks ready, Comment-only, Needs changes before merge, or Not enough context
Separates blocking findings from non-blocking follow-up rather than presenting one flat list
Cites a file path for each finding and names the concrete consequence instead of suggesting an improvement in the abstract
Omits style, formatting, and naming comments unless they affect correctness, security, data integrity, or maintainability
Keeps references/design-lens.md optional and only uses it when it materially changes architecture, API, platform, or boundary critique
Applies at most three named principles rather than cataloging every law that could apply
States which validation ran, or names exactly what was missing, without implying it passed

evals.prompt: Review a PR where the diff looks correct but there is insufficient evidence to evaluate whether the central behavior works or is safe. Decide what the smallest concrete ask is before merge.
evals.expected_output: A principal-engineer review that distinguishes finished-looking output from reviewable reasoning, avoids process theater, and asks for concrete evidence only when it affects correctness, safety, rollback, or scope.
assertions: Checks whether the PR makes why, approach, validation, uncertainty, and rediscovery notes visible enough to review
Does not require transcript dumps or broad process when missing reasoning is not material
Raises missing reasoning as blocking only when correctness, safety, rollback, or scope cannot be evaluated from available evidence
Recommends a durable context improvement when the missing reasoning is likely to recur

evals.expected_output: A read-only principal-engineer review package for the newest eligible direct request, or the newest eligible team request when no direct request qualifies. An explicit no-eligible-request result is also valid. The first pass stops before drafting or posting a GitHub response.
assertions: Resolves the authenticated GitHub login and discovers candidates without asking the user for a PR URL
Searches the direct-review queue first and only searches the broader team-capable queue when no direct request qualifies
Considers only open, non-draft PRs from non-archived repositories that the authenticated user has not reviewed
Prioritizes the newest eligible direct request, then the newest eligible team request
Selects an older eligible direct request over a newer eligible team request
Validates the selected PR before beginning the AI review step and fails closed on discovery or validation errors
Returns the selected PR identity, selection reason, decision, material findings, evidence, useful non-blocking feedback, and uncertainty
Includes a compact orientation and context map by default unless earlier conversation demonstrates the relevant system context
Treats the review decision as analysis only and stops for human review before drafting review-comment prose, choosing a GitHub disposition, or mutating GitHub

evals.prompt: Review Fixture A in examples/closure-review-fixtures.md and decide whether the production incident fix is ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: A high-risk review that traces the affected collection through the real execution path, finds the equivalent downstream argument-expansion hazard, and blocks merge with checkable evidence.
assertions: Classifies production incident and scale-limit remediation as high-risk
Names the changed invariant or failure mechanism instead of reviewing only the changed syntax
Cites the downstream consumer and the equivalent spread hazard with checkable evidence
Explains why the helper-only test is a proxy rather than proof of the integration path
Returns Needs changes before merge rather than Looks ready

evals.prompt: Review Fixture B in examples/closure-review-fixtures.md and decide whether the selective cache change is safe to deploy behind its disabled flag.
evals.expected_output: A high-risk structural and operational-contract review that finds the ancestry-dependent telemetry regression and blocks merge.
assertions: Treats structural runtime composition and rollout-critical telemetry as high-risk
Names ancestry order as the changed implicit contract
Inspects consumers of ancestry or class identity rather than only the prepended module behavior
Compares the emitted telemetry tag with the dashboard filter
Returns Needs changes before merge with path or contract evidence

evals.prompt: Review Fixture C in examples/closure-review-fixtures.md and decide whether the retry-logging refactor preserves existing behavior. Keep the review proportional and evidence-based.
evals.expected_output: A behavior-sensitive or high-risk review that generalizes the changed-invariant rule to a novel implicit contract without tracing unrelated application paths.
assertions: Identifies identity metadata as the changed implicit contract
Inspects the serializer as a consumer of that contract
Requires checkable path and search evidence before claiming closure
Keeps the trace bounded to relevant consumers
Does not rely only on the spread or ancestry examples

evals.prompt: Review this PR scenario and decide whether it is ready to merge. The PR adds a shadow worker beside the legacy poller. `shadow_worker_enabled` will be enabled during validation, while `shadow_live_actions_enabled` stays off until a later cutover decision. The code always enqueues the legacy poll and additionally enqueues the shadow when `shadow_worker_enabled` is on. In `retry_failed_scan`, the shadow records a metric and returns unless `shadow_live_actions_enabled` is on; when on, it calls `Scanner.start_scan` and re-enqueues itself. A focused test deliberately asserts that enabling live actions calls `Scanner.start_scan`, while the legacy path remains present. The rollout notes say to validate the no-op shadow first and settle production ownership before enabling live actions, but do not say whether duplicate replacement scans during a temporary dual-live phase are intended.
evals.expected_output: A calibrated review that treats the duplicate live-action path as deliberate but ambiguous activation-time behavior, asks for intent if needed, and does not turn a dormant flag concern into a merge blocker.
assertions: Uses rollout notes, feature-flag defaults, and tests as evidence of intended behavior
Classifies duplicate replacement scans as activation-time rather than merge-time under the stated rollout
Asks a narrow intent question instead of asserting an ambiguous deliberate behavior is a proven bug
Distinguishes safe to merge from safe to enable
Returns Looks ready or Comment-only unless additional evidence makes the live-action path reachable now

evals.prompt: Invoke the principal-engineer-review skill before answering. No PR, diff, or repository tools are supplied. Describe the exact review routing for a high-risk migration PR that already includes a fresh opposite-provider critique covering rollback, compatibility, and data integrity. Explain how the existing critique changes reviewer selection and do not claim a readiness decision.
evals.expected_output: A principal-engineer review plan that reuses the fresh independent critique, verifies its material claims against repository evidence when available, and does not launch a duplicate rubber-duck reviewer.
assertions: Recognizes that the fresh same-scope opposite-provider critique satisfies the independent-review need
Does not launch another rubber-duck reviewer for rollback, compatibility, or data integrity
Requires verification of material critique claims against the diff, tests, and documented runtime contracts
Uses a third model only if a consequential disagreement remains after direct verification
Does not claim a readiness decision without the PR evidence

evals.prompt: Help me understand this PR well enough to review it. I am a capable junior engineer, but I have no context on this repository. The PR changes a retry counter so normal polling and real failures no longer share the same budget.
evals.expected_output: A compact guided review that starts with purpose and before/after behavior, defines only the necessary concepts, presents material findings with evidence, and makes deeper conversational paths obvious without dumping a repository tour.
assertions: Treats junior engineer as limited system context rather than limited technical ability
Explains the business purpose and before/after behavior before relying on repository-specific terminology
Places orientation before the decision and findings because the user has no demonstrated context
Provides a concrete mental model of the relevant execution or data path
Defines only terms needed to understand the material findings
Separates verified facts, interpretation, and unresolved questions
Keeps the initial response compact rather than providing a file-by-file walkthrough
Offers relevant deeper paths such as tracing execution, inspecting tests, comparing alternatives, or revisiting a finding
Does not draft feedback or ask for a GitHub review disposition

evals.prompt: I already understand the request path, the retry scheduler, and why polling must not consume the failure budget. Review whether the cleanup ordering preserves that invariant.
evals.expected_output: An adaptive review that recognizes the user's demonstrated context, skips basic teaching, and focuses on the decision, evidence, cleanup ordering, and remaining uncertainty.
assertions: Recognizes the concepts the user has already demonstrated
Does not repeat the request-path or retry-counter mental model
Leads with the decision and evidence relevant to cleanup ordering because the user already has context
Explains only new concepts that materially affect the finding
Keeps deeper explanation available on demand

evals.prompt: Trace the execution path behind the first blocking finding and explain why the focused unit test does not prove the production behavior.
evals.expected_output: A focused pair-partner deep dive into one finding that walks the relevant path, distinguishes proxy coverage from integration evidence, and names unavailable evidence without guessing.
assertions: Deepens only the requested finding rather than repeating the full review
Walks the relevant execution path in order
Connects each material step to checkable evidence
Explains why the unit test is a proxy rather than proof of the production path
Names the smallest missing test or runtime evidence that would close the question

evals.prompt: I think your blocking finding is wrong because the dangerous path is behind a disabled flag. Re-check it against the rollout and tests.
evals.expected_output: A non-defensive re-evaluation that verifies reachability, updates the finding when warranted, and distinguishes safe to merge from safe to enable.
assertions: Re-checks feature-flag defaults, rollout notes, tests, and runtime reachability
Updates, downgrades, or withdraws the finding when the evidence warrants it
Distinguishes merge-time from activation-time risk
Does not defend the original conclusion based on authority
States what remains uncertain after the re-check

evals.prompt: The review explanation makes sense. Turn the blocking finding into a concise review comment.
evals.expected_output: A concise standalone review comment drafted from the established evidence without repeating the full explanation or posting.
assertions: Recognizes that the user has demonstrated understanding
Drafts directly from the established review evidence
Does not repeat the full PR orientation
Includes the concrete consequence and practical safer path
Uses path and line evidence when available
Does not post or choose a disposition

evals.prompt: Post this principal-engineer review as a request for changes.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained posting safety gate that requires the exact draft, repository-qualified target, request-changes disposition, freshness check, privacy scan, and explicit approval before any GitHub write.
assertions: Shows or identifies the exact review text covered by approval
Requires a full repository-qualified PR URL
Requires explicit approval of the request-changes disposition
Preserves head-SHA freshness and external-text privacy validation before any write

evals.prompt: Using only this supplied evidence, produce the completed review package and stop before drafting feedback. Target: https://github.com/example/app/pull/42, head abc123. Localized authorization flaw: app/controllers/jobs_controller.rb line 42 returns raw job arguments to every caller authenticated by a shared HMAC; repository policy says this endpoint may expose only job ID and readiness; tests prove the raw payload response. Cross-cutting observability concern: the new controller, worker, and client paths emit no metric distinguishing authorization rejection from queue lookup failure; this is non-blocking because existing logs still identify failures. Validation performed: focused tests passed. No external write.
evals.expected_output: The review includes the normal human-readable package plus a structured handoff with stable finding identities, blocking status, confidence, evidence separated from interpretation, placement guidance, and a non-authorizing disposition suggestion.
assertions: Includes one of the four allowed review decisions
Includes a structured handoff after the human-readable analysis
Assigns a stable findingId to each finding
Marks the authorization flaw blocking and the observability concern non-blocking
Separates verifiedFact, interpretation, uncertainty, consequence, and recommendedNextStep
Uses inline placement only for the localized finding with a verified path and line
Uses summary placement for the cross-cutting finding
Includes a suggestedDisposition that is explicitly not posting authorization
Records the focused tests as passed without inventing additional validation
Treats the structured handoff as internal coordination data rather than recipient-facing text
Does not draft polished review comments or mutate GitHub

evals.prompt: Use principal-engineer-review on this fully supplied change program; no repository lookup is needed. PR A is https://github.com/example/app/pull/1, targets main at SHA 0000, has head SHA aaaa, and adds an inert repository-scoped moderation state model. PR B is https://github.com/example/app/pull/2, targets PR A at SHA aaaa, has head SHA bbbb, and adds build and private-auth enforcement. PR C is https://github.com/example/app/pull/3, targets PR B at SHA bbbb, has head SHA cccc, and adds the operator action that writes the state. A separate public-serving repository must reject the state before the promised hard takedown is complete, but no linked PR exists there. PR D is https://github.com/example/app/pull/4, targets PR C at SHA cccc, has head SHA dddd, and is a read-only indicator even though it only depends on PR A. The current review target is PR A. Produce the completed review package and structured handoff. Explain whether PR A can merge, whether the program can activate, how PR D should be sequenced, and what stack evidence must be recorded. Do not post anything.
evals.expected_output: A stack-aware review that permits the sound inert foundation, blocks program activation on the missing public-serving prerequisite, identifies the incorrectly sequenced indicator, and records the dependency and activation graph without treating the dependent branch chain as an atomic native stack.
assertions: Sets changeProgram.relationship to dependent-branch-chain or linked-change-program rather than inventing another label or assuming native stack guarantees
Reviews the layer delta, cumulative program result, and intermediate merge or deployment states separately
Does not reject PR A solely because the inert foundation does not deliver the final takedown by itself
Identifies PR C as the activation or keystone layer and blocks activation until public serving enforces the state
Assigns the missing public-serving behavior as a cross-repository prerequisite rather than a defect owned by PR A
Recommends that PR D depend directly on PR A because it does not require PR B or PR C
Requires current head and parent SHAs plus an explicit diff basis so review freshness survives restacking
Includes changeProgram evidence and finding fields including findingId, programStatus, owningTarget, reachability, and resolvedUpstack
Represents the missing public-serving change as a crossRepositoryPrerequisite whose targetUrl may be null
Reports unperformed validation in validation.missing instead of leaving validation empty
Avoids duplicating the same program-wide finding as a blocking comment on every PR
Makes no GitHub mutation

evals.prompt: Use principal-engineer-review to draft this established blocking finding as a concise review comment. The private review conversation corrected our first theory after tracing the retry path. The PR author has only seen the PR and its tests. Finding: `src/retry_cleanup.ts:42` deletes jobs using one counter that still combines normal polling with real failures, so cleanup can remove work that has not failed. Recommended safer sequence: split the polling and failure counters before running cleanup.
evals.expected_output: A concise standalone review comment that uses the corrected analysis without implying the PR author participated in the private investigation.
assertions: Includes the concrete consequence and safer sequence
Uses the supplied path and line
Does not mention the private conversation, first theory, correction process, or time spent investigating
Does not use phrases such as as we discussed, after digging further, or false-inclusive we
Contains no dangling references that require the private conversation
Does not post or choose a disposition
